Bug_Details:
This assertion will always fail or succeed. If a test subject and the argument to isEqualTo are the same instance (e.g.
assertThat(x).isEqualTo(x)), then the assertion will always pass. Truth
implements isEqualTo using [Objects#equal] , which tests its arguments for
reference equality and returns true without calling equals() if both arguments
are the same instance. To test the implementation of an equals method, use
Guava’s EqualsTester.
Bug_Explanation: The code demonstrates a self-assertion bug where the method checkEquality checks if an object is equal to itself. This will always return true because it uses Objects.equals which tests for reference equality before calling equals().
Trigger_Explanation: The test case calls the 'showBug' method which internally triggers the self-assertion bug. The method showBug uses an object to check equality against itself, which always returns true due to reference equality. The test expects a false result, thereby triggering the bug.
